**7. PUBLIC HEARING PROCEEDINGS**

Pursuant to Section 82 of the *Planning and Environment Act 1987*, a public hearing was held on Thursday, 20 August 2026, commencing at 10:00 am at the Council Chambers, 48 MacKenzie Street, Mooroopna. The hearing was conducted by an independent Planning Panel comprising Ms P. Hartley (Chair) and Mr D. O'Keefe (Panel Member). Council officers in attendance were Mr T. Nguyen (Senior Planner, presenting), Ms J. Kowalski (Manager Planning Services) and Mr R. Singh (Legal Counsel).

The purpose of the hearing was to consider submissions received in response to the advertising of Planning Application PA-2026-118 for the development of a cold storage warehouse and associated infrastructure at 117 Sandhill Road, Kialla West (Lot 2 on PS 634218Y). A total of 14 submissions were received during the public notification period, of which 12 were objections, one was a support submission, and one was a late submission accepted by the Panel at the commencement of the hearing.

**7.1 Applicant Presentation**

The Applicant, represented by Mr A. Ferraro of Ferraro Planning Group, presented an overview of the proposal. Mr Ferraro outlined the key elements of the development, including the construction of a 4,850 square metre cold storage facility with an adjoining 620 square metre office and staff amenities area. He noted that the facility would operate 24 hours a day, seven days a week, with refrigeration plant operating continuously. The Applicant confirmed that the proposed finished floor level of RL 108.55 m AHD would be maintained as per the plans submitted, and that all stormwater detention measures would be constructed in accordance with the conditions proposed by Goulburn-Murray Water.

Mr Ferraro also addressed concerns raised in submissions regarding truck movements. He stated that the Applicant had agreed to enter into a Section 173 Agreement with Council to ensure that all trucks entering or leaving the site travel via Sandhill Road to the Midland Highway, and shall not use local roads in the Kialla West residential area. He confirmed that the Applicant had no objection to the conditions proposed by VicRoads, including the requirement for a road safety audit prior to commencement of works.

**7.2 Submitter Statements**

The following objectors presented oral submissions to the Panel:

**Mrs. B. Thompson (Submission 1)** – Resident of 42 Kialla Lakes Drive, Kialla West. Mrs. Thompson raised concerns regarding increased heavy vehicle movements along Sandhill Road, particularly during night-time hours. She stated that the road currently experiences minimal traffic after 8:00 pm and that the proposed 24-hour operation would result in unacceptable noise disturbance for nearby residents. She also queried whether the road pavement was designed to accommodate the expected volume of B-double trucks.

**Mr. P. O'Sullivan (Submission 4)** – Resident of 19 Warralite Court, Kialla West. Mr. O'Sullivan objected on the grounds of potential groundwater contamination from the refrigeration system. He noted that the site is located within a floodplain and expressed concern that any leak of refrigerants or other chemicals could affect local water quality. He requested that the Panel recommend additional conditions requiring regular maintenance and monitoring of the refrigeration plant.

**9. PANEL HEARING – SUMMARY OF PROCEEDINGS AND OUTCOME**

**9.1 Hearing Dates and Venue**

The Panel hearing was held over two days, 28 and 29 July 2026, at the Council Chambers, 48 McLennan Street, Mooroopna. The hearing was conducted pursuant to Division 1 of Part 3 of the *Planning and Environment Act 1987*.

**9.2 Parties to the Hearing**

The purpose of this amendment is to provide a formal statement of the planned cold storage capacity for the record and to assist Council officers and referral authorities in assessing the transport and logistics implications of the development.

**7. PUBLIC HEARING PROCEEDINGS**

Pursuant to Section 82 of the *Planning and Environment Act 1987*, a public hearing was held on Thursday, 20 August 2026, commencing at 10:00 am at the Council Chambers, 48 MacKenzie Street, Mooroopna. The hearing was conducted by an independent Planning Panel comprising Ms P. Hartley (Chair) and Mr D. O'Keefe (Panel Member). Council officers in attendance were Mr T. Nguyen (Senior Planner, presenting), Ms J. Kowalski (Manager Planning Services) and Mr R. Singh (Legal Counsel).

The purpose of the hearing was to consider submissions received in response to the advertising of Planning Application PA-2026-118 for the development of a cold storage warehouse and associated infrastructure at 117 Sandhill Road, Kialla West (Lot 2 on PS 634218Y). A total of 14 submissions were received during the public notification period, of which 12 were objections, one was a support submission, and one was a late submission accepted by the Panel at the commencement of the hearing.

**7.1 Applicant Presentation**

The Applicant, represented by Mr A. Ferraro of Ferraro Planning Group, presented an overview of the proposal. Mr Ferraro outlined the key elements of the development, including the construction of a 4,850 square metre cold storage facility with an adjoining 620 square metre office and staff amenities area. He noted that the facility would operate 24 hours a day, seven days a week, with refrigeration plant operating continuously. The Applicant confirmed that the proposed finished floor level of RL 108.55 m AHD would be maintained as per the plans submitted, and that all stormwater detention measures would be constructed in accordance with the conditions proposed by Goulburn-Murray Water.

Mr Ferraro also addressed concerns raised in submissions regarding truck movements. He stated that the Applicant had agreed to enter into a Section 173 Agreement with Council to ensure that all trucks entering or leaving the site travel via Sandhill Road to the Midland Highway, and shall not use local roads in the Kialla West residential area. He confirmed that the Applicant had no objection to the conditions proposed by VicRoads, including the requirement for a road safety audit prior to commencement of works.

**7.2 Submitter Statements**

The following objectors presented oral submissions to the Panel:

**Mrs. B. Thompson (Submission 1)** – Resident of 42 Kialla Lakes Drive, Kialla West. Mrs. Thompson raised concerns regarding increased heavy vehicle movements along Sandhill Road, particularly during night-time hours. She stated that the road currently experiences minimal traffic after 8:00 pm and that the proposed 24-hour operation would result in unacceptable noise disturbance for nearby residents. She also queried whether the road pavement was designed to accommodate the expected volume of B-double trucks.

**Mr. P. O'Sullivan (Submission 4)** – Resident of 19 Warralite Court, Kialla West. Mr. O'Sullivan objected on the grounds of potential groundwater contamination from the refrigeration system. He noted that the site is located within a floodplain and expressed concern that any leak of refrigerants or other chemicals could affect local water quality. He requested that the Panel recommend additional conditions requiring regular maintenance and monitoring of the refrigeration plant.
